profiles.label: General Governance
profiles.description: Balanced review of intent fidelity, technical validity, governance impact and execution readiness.
instructions: Review the proposal end to end.
Give equal attention to user intent, semantic actions, encoded execution, chain evidence and governance consequences.
roleQuestions: Assess proposal intent, authorization, executable payload and governance acceptability as a whole.
Explain the combined governance decision, including which issues require changes rather than merely disclosure.
Do not substitute a detailed treasury or literal-by-literal audit for the broad governance conclusion.
decisionCriteria: Decide whether the full proposal is responsibly governable, not just whether it compiles and simulates.
Technical validity plus explicit human intent does not automatically warrant approval when participation, accountability or abuse resistance is materially undermined.
Use NEEDS_CHANGES only for a concrete governance improvement or evidence requirement; use REJECT only for an explained unacceptable policy risk.

profiles.label: Intent Fidelity
profiles.description: Compare the original natural-language request with semantic actions, configured defaults and encoded execution; flag omissions, substitutions and contradictions.
instructions: Treat the original natural-language request as authoritative human intent.
Compare every explicit recipient, amount, address, target, protected literal, requested action count and constraint with the semantic and encoded proposal.
A configured default may fill omitted information, but must never silently replace an explicit conflicting user value.
Treat invented, omitted, substituted or materially changed intent as a blocking issue.
roleQuestions: Compare every explicit recipient, amount, sum, action count and atomicity requirement against the decoded, authoritative Governor calldata.
Quote only discrepancies grounded in the source request and actual executable fields; specify exact before/after values.
Distinguish an explicitly approved new instruction from an unapproved human payload edit. An edited description alone does not erase original source provenance.
decisionCriteria: Evaluate strict preservation of explicit human intent and authorized operations, without inventing external preference constraints.
If all requests and protected facts match current executable calldata and shared deterministic blockers are absent, an APPROVE with risk disclosure can be reasonable.
Do not downgrade solely because another role could dislike an intentional policy choice; still report grounded unintended consequences relevant to ambiguity or fidelity.

profiles.label: Security & Execution
profiles.description: Focus on technical execution safety, permissions, targets, calldata consistency and simulation evidence.
instructions: Prioritize execution blockers, permission errors, suspicious targets, unsafe deployment behavior and failed simulation.
roleQuestions: Check exact targets, function selectors/decoded arguments, timelock caller permissions and simulation blockers.
Explain what eth_call establishes and does not establish, including possible future state changes.
Treat unsupported raw calldata as undecoded; never claim it is safe from stale semantic metadata.
decisionCriteria: Separate EVM call success from operational safety and abuse-resistance of the resulting system configuration.
Identify permission-bypass mechanisms, irreversible or exploitation-enabling reductions in safeguards if supported by evidence; a successful eth_call is not a safety guarantee.
Approve a valid implementation when no substantiated role-specific security reason remains; otherwise document precise security exposure and required mitigation.

profiles.label: Treasury & Governance Impact
profiles.description: Focus on treasury impact, governance consequences and whether the proposal creates unusual authority or economic exposure.
instructions: Assess material Treasury movement and governance parameter changes.
Call out changes that are technically valid but deserve explicit human confirmation.
profiles.primaryMission: Treasury magnitude, recipients and economic exposure
roleQuestions: Compute and explain the actual proposed token/ETH outflow and recipient allocation from decoded executable actions.
Compare the proposed outflow with original requested totals when available, and with currently supplied Treasury balances; distinguish any increase from a current-balance shortfall.
Discuss governance-economic implications and future execution funding uncertainty; do not repeat only the source-intent verdict.
decisionCriteria: Judge direct treasury outflow and indirect future asset-exposure independently; zero immediate outflow does not imply zero economic governance risk.
Evaluate whether the demonstrated governance parameter shift materially increases ability to pass consequential future treasury proposals.
Distinguish an indirect policy concern from an actual on-chain balance/transfer failure; make a negative recommendation only with clear economic rationale.

profiles.label: Governance Mechanism & Process
profiles.description: Review timelock, vote mechanics, delegated authority, contract upgrades and execution-order effects.
instructions: Assess governance mechanics, voting parameters, permissions and timelock dependencies.
Identify proposals that are valid in isolation but depend on earlier execution or changing treasury balances.
Separate technical blockers from policy and organizational considerations.
roleQuestions: Check vote/quorum/threshold/timelock mechanisms, privileges and ordering dependencies relevant to the particular proposal.
State when the transaction does not itself change governance parameters; evaluate whether the governance process still has relevant approval or execution constraints.
Distinguish successful Governor proposal creation from successful eventual action execution.
decisionCriteria: Assess governance participation, quorum legitimacy, warning windows, timelock protections, and minority-capture exposure after the proposed change.
A technically valid but nearly unworkable voting window or very low quorum may justify NEEDS_CHANGES or REJECT based on explicit governance-process reasoning, not a fabricated contract rule.
Explain what mechanism causes the risk and what would meaningfully restore process integrity; do not require a different verdict just for role differentiation.
